overview: Tenacity 6.0's Flight is a nine-mode dispatcher on a single MotionEvent pre handler, with a packet-receive handler reserved for the Mineland launch sequence. Vanilla pins motionY to 3, -3 or 0 by key and re-applies a horizontal speed of 3 every tick while stamping onGround true; HvH Mode does the same at 5 blocks per tick; BlocksMC flies at speed 5 with motionY 0.1, auto-disables after 7 seconds or 2 blocks of fall, and exploits knockback at hurtTime above 20; Vulcan claims abilities flight through sendPlayerAbilities with allowFlying and isFlying set; Negativity Fast runs a 31-packet damage ritual then pins speed 9.9; Mineland Jank alternates timer 2.5 jumps with drift descents; and Mineland Fling cancels the first S08 teleport, captures a server S12 velocity as its launch and then rides speed 3 with periodic 0.42 lifts. Grim and NCP are empty cases, Verus Funny is empty, and the packetList buffer is cleared and flushed but never populated, so its disable-time flush is inert.

sections.p: The motion handler switches on the ModeSetting's current mode. Grim and NCP are empty cases, so selecting them does nothing; Verus Fast is the only Verus subtype with code, Funny is empty; and the receive handler's Watchdog branch is unreachable because Watchdog is not a registered mode. The packetList field is cleared on enable and iterated on disable, but no code path ever adds to it, so the flush that would replay buffered packets is dead. The local tickCounter in Verus Fast is declared and incremented inside the event, so it resets to zero every call and the tickCounter > 30 jump gate never fires.

Vanilla stamps onGround true, then sets motionY to 3, -3 or 0 from the space and shift keys and calls MovementUtil.setSpeed(3) three times per tick, a redundant re-pin. HvH Mode pins motionY to 5, -5 or 0 and speed 5, zeroing all motion when no key is held. BlocksMC pins speed 5 with motionY 0.1, forces sprint, sends player abilities and stamps onGround false, disables itself when fall distance exceeds 2 or the 7-second timer elapses, and in the knockback branch, when hurtTime is above 20 and the player is airborne, pins speed 9.972 with motionY 0.1. Negativity Fast ends with speed 9.9, and Infinite is only a motionY zero. Every one of these modes is a magnitude pin the server never granted.

sections.h: Timer abuse and the damage ritual
sections.p: Verus Fast alternates the global timer between a slow band (random 0.04 to 0.14 every 10 ticks) and a fast band (random 4.84 to 5.64 otherwise), a sustained 5x speed-up that scales the whole outgoing stream; Mineland Jank runs timer 2.5 with periodic jumps and a speed-20 spike. Negativity Fast performs the classic fall-damage ritual on enable: 15 iterations of a C04PacketPlayerPosition at y plus 0.3 and y plus 0.1, both onGround false, followed by a y plus 0.1 claim with onGround true, 31 packets in a single tick, then flight at speed 9.9. Mineland Fling is the receive-side mode: it cancels the first S08 teleport, waits for a server S12 velocity with motionY over 0.1 (the anticheat's knockback launch), then flies with event y drops of 0.9 and periodic 0.42 lifts, using getDirection() for both the yaw and the pitch of the horizontal push.

files.label: FlightModule.java (module)
files.explanation:
The module is the onMotionEvent consumer with the mode switch, plus onReceivePacket for the Mineland sequence and the enable/disable state machine. The constructor wires the subtype settings to their parents (Mineland, Verus, Negativity), and the module's suffix updates from a third handler. onEnable snapshots the server position, clears the dead packetList, resets damage and teleported, and prints mode-specific warnings; onDisable restores the timer, clears the flying capabilities, zeroes motion and flushes the never-populated buffer.

The interesting mechanics are the Negativity ritual (31 C04s in one tick with the hurtTime 30 spoof that fakes knockback damage), the Verus timer bands (slow every 10 ticks, fast otherwise), and the Mineland Fling receive logic, which turns the server's own knockback into the launch by capturing the S12 velocity and setting teleported once it arrives. The mode.isMode checks in the receive handler use strings that never match the registered modes (Negativity damage fast, Watchdog), so only the Mineland branch can run.

files.label: MovementUtil.java (speed writers)
files.explanation:
MovementUtil.setSpeed resolves the movement input into a yaw through getDirection and writes motionX and motionZ as the yaw components times the given speed, returning early when no input key is held. Every mode's horizontal pin runs through it, from Vanilla's 3 to Negativity's 9.9, and the two-argument overload blends toward the current speed by a strafe percentage.

getSpeed reads the horizontal magnitude for the Mineland Jank spike condition (speed above 3 triggers the speed-20 burst), and getAllowedHDistNCP mirrors the NCP horizontal allowance from walk speed and potions, which the module never actually uses. The class is the shared writer for Tenacity's movement family, so the flight pins are the same writes a Tenacity speed module would make.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly's horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation's sprint prediction, roughly 0.31 blocks per tick on a stock server, and its vertical allowance from vDistRel, which seeds from the previous move's momentum and accepts only the named envelopes (zero-y ground, jump, step, riptide). Ground state is ray-traced from the block cache, so the onGround true stamps Vanilla and Vulcan write mean nothing to it. The violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) plus max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100 with a set-back.

Every pin mode violates on the first move. Vanilla's motionY 3 is a 3-block rise against a momentum seed, yDistanceAboveLimit near 2.6, while its speed 3 pin beats the sprint prediction by about 2.7, so the horizontal side alone is a violation in the 270 range per tick; HvH Mode's 5-block pins are worse on both axes. Negativity's speed 9.9 is roughly 32 times the prediction, and the 31-packet ritual that precedes it delivers the position outlier of the y plus 0.3 and y plus 0.1 stack, which vDistRel reads as a climb. The 0.42 periodic lifts in Mineland Fling are the one legal vertical move in the module, and the sustained flight around them is not.

countering.label: Flight (hover, ascension, glide)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight checks the vertical profile of every move. The hover check fires when both the last and current vertical speeds are exactly zero and airTicks passes maxHover, which is the resting state of Vanilla (motionY 0 in air) and HvH Mode (motionY 0 with no key held). The ascension branch flags any rise above getMaxJump as ascending_vertical, and the descending branch compares the vertical change against a gravity polynomial.

Vanilla's motionY 3 and HvH Mode's motionY 5 exceed the jump cap on the first rising move, so ascending_vertical fires immediately; the hover state between key presses crosses the maxHover air-time threshold once the player stops tapping; and the abrupt 3-to-0 and 5-to-0 switches produce glide deltas that never match the expected gravity curve. BlocksMC's motionY 0.1 drift is outside the model too, since a nonzero constant vertical in air matches neither the hover zero nor the gravity polynomial. The knockback branch's 9.972 pin rides a motionY 0.1 that the descent check reads as a violation on the first airborne move.

countering.label: Fly (predicted-velocity discrepancy)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly runs a per-player vertical simulation: in air the predicted velocity is (previous estimated velocity minus 0.08) times 0.98, integrated into an estimated position, and the reported Y is compared against it; any discrepancy over 0.0001 punishes and rubber-bands. On a reported ground contact the check also requires the reported Y to fall between the previous Y and the estimated position.

The vertical pins are instant failures. Vanilla's motionY 3 and HvH Mode's motionY 5 report a rise of 3 or 5 blocks against a predicted fall of about 0.0784 per tick, a discrepancy measured in whole blocks on the first move; the hover state, where motion is zero in air, diverges from the predicted fall within two ticks. Negativity's onGround true stamp over open air fails the landing-path check, since the reported Y is nowhere near the estimated descent path. Mineland Fling's event y drops of 0.9 and periodic 0.42 lifts are the closest thing to a legal profile in the module, but the sustained speed 3 horizontal flight around them still leaves the vertical model measuring a stream that never matches gravity.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
MorePackets scores serverbound move packets in 500ms buckets against a 22-per-second ceiling with 20 ideal, plus a half-second burst path (15 packets default, direct violation at 10). It is invoked per move from MovingListener, so accelerated streams and concentrated bursts both register.

The Negativity Fast ritual is a textbook burst: 31 C04s in a single tick, three times the burst path's direct-violation count of 10, so the violation fires the moment the ritual lands and the set-back cancels the launch. The timer modes register on the sustained side: Verus Fast's 4.84-to-5.64 timer band scales a 20-per-second stream to roughly 100 packets per second, and Mineland Jank's timer 2.5 doubles it, both far past the window ceiling for as long as the mode runs. The only mode that stays under the rate checks is Infinite, which pins motionY 0 and sends one C03 per tick, and it is exactly the mode that does nothing on the wire.
